q: The geometric mean of two distributions P, Q in information geometry is the point M on the e-geodesic from P to Q at t=1/2, which equals:
exp: The e-geodesic midpoint (exponential barycenter): p_t ∝ p(x)^{1-t} q(x)^t. At t=1/2: m(x) ∝ √(p(x)q(x)) (geometric mean, normalised). The m-geodesic midpoint is the arithmetic mean (p+q)/2. These differ—the two geodesics give different interpolations.
